sites.rationale: P2Y14 has no signal peptide (raw topology 'O' from residue 1) and its sole extracellular terminus is the N-terminus (residues 1–23); the C-terminus (299–338) is intracellular. Because exactly one extracellular terminus exists, the topology_derived rule places the HA tag as a prepend before residue 1 (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M). The 23-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample separation from TM1 (which begins at residue 24), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-boundary constraint. No residue number was named in the ledger, so cited_tag_residue is null and the position is topology-derived, not validated. Full-length human P2Y14 cloned into pcDNA3 with an HA tag and expressed in HEK293 cells for functional studies (PMC10642967). No residue number is stated in the ledger.

sources.claim: Human P2Y14 or P2Y12 was cloned into a pcDNA3 vector with HA tag for expression in HEK293 cells.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports a full-length HA-tagged P2Y14 construct in HEK293 cells but names no insertion residue and gives no explicit surface-detection or functional assay result. The position is derived from topology: the N-terminus (1–23) is the sole extracellular terminus (no signal peptide; C-terminus is intracellular). ECL1 (80–95), ECL2 (161–185), and ECL3 (257–276) are extracellular loops but are not termini, so the topology_derived rule does not extend to them without a named residue or loop. No other ledger lines ground any ECL insertion. C14 in the N-terminal domain is noted but lies downstream of the prepend junction and does not disqualify the site.
